subject: general
question: The income of Raman is ₹70,000. He saves 26% of his income. If his income increases by 32% and expenditure increases by 45%, then his savings will:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Income = 70000, Savings = 26% ⇒ Expenditure = 74%

New Income = 70000 × 1.32 = 92400

New Expenditure = 70000 × 0.74 × 1.45 = 75110

New Savings = 92400 − 75110 = 17290

**∴ Decrease in savings = 18200 − 17290 = 910**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Income = 70000, Savings = 26%

**Formula used:**

Savings = Income − Expenditure

**Calculation:**

⇒ Savings = 26% of 70000 = 18200

⇒ Expenditure = 70000 − 18200 = 51800

⇒ New Income = 70000 × 1.32 = 92400

⇒ New Expenditure = 51800 × 1.45 = 75110

⇒ New Savings = 92400 − 75110 = 17290

⇒ Change = 17290 − 18200 = −910

**∴ The savings decrease by ₹910.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Increase Formula

New Value = Original × (1 + rate/100)

Savings Concept

Savings = Income − Expenditure

Key Insight

If expenditure rises faster than income, savings will decrease.
